Patient: I'm 45 years old and male. I'm here because I've been having this pain on the right side of my belly under my ribs for several weeks, and even after changing my diet to avoid high-fat foods, the pain is still really bad sometimes.
Doctor: Can you describe the nature of the pain (e.g., sharp, dull, burning), its radiation (e.g., to the back or shoulder), and whether it is associated with any specific activities or meals?
Patient: The pain feels like a squeezing, severe pain, and it's right under my ribs on the right side. It comes and goes, but when it does come, it's really bad and I get nauseated. It usually happens after I eat, either right away or a couple of hours later.
Doctor: Have you experienced any episodes of jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools during this time? Have you had any recent weight loss or changes in bowel habits?
Patient: No, I haven't had any jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools. I haven't lost any weight recently, and my bowel habits haven't changed much.
Doctor: Have you experienced any fever, chills, or changes in bowel habits such as diarrhea or constipation associated with the pain?
Patient: I haven't had any fever or chills with the pain, and my bowel habits haven't really changed. I do get nauseated sometimes, but I haven't vomited.
Doctor: Has the patient experienced any radiation of the pain to the back, shoulder, or right shoulder? Additionally, has there been any history of similar episodes or family history of gallbladder disease?
Patient: The pain doesn't radiate to my back or shoulder, just stays right under my ribs on the right side. Both my mom and dad had gallbladder issues and had their gallbladders removed, so there's a family history of it.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies or blood tests to evaluate the cause of your right upper quadrant pain?
